answer: A durable anti-Sybil test could use anchored place-keeping on a mesa. Each applicant adopts one meadow plot on a mesa rim and sets a numbered anchor stone at its corner, then records the plot's wildflowers, grazing signs, and erosion each month for a full year. Neighbors walk the same transects and compare notes, photos, and weather logs, so a claimed plot must match its real seasons. Creating dozens of fake identities would mean hiking to dozens of distant mesas and tending each plot through drought and frost, while a genuine local keeper only keeps visiting land they already know.
